## 1. D:L1180: the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge, at primaries

| Question | Answer | Grade |
|---|---|---|
| What happened | The road section's main arched span and the deck beneath it fell into the Kerch Strait after the second of two Ukrainian attacks. The parallel rail bridge stands with a damaged arch. | **CONFIRMED.** The Russian Transport Ministry suspended road and rail traffic ("specialists are assessing the damage", no injuries, preliminary). Khusnullin says the damage is assessed. Peskov says it "will be restored and will be even better than before". Reuters verified images of the arch in the water, and CNN geolocated the deck in the water. These are independent chains. |
| When | First hit 11/16 ~05:38 local: an arch shifted ~15 degrees and road traffic stopped ~16 hours; the Kremlin called it "minor". Collapse in the second attack, overnight 11/16-17. | CONFIRMED (dates). The exact time of the second attack is not given. |
| Status 11/18 | Road fully closed (Mintrans via Interfax). Rail restored on one track 11/17, first train 13:04 Moscow (Vedomosti citing Mintrans; Aksyonov). Ferries carry most traffic. | CONFIRMED |
| Span length, weapons, "seventh phase" | 227 m (eyewitness footage via Moscow Times) vs >270 m (Dnipro Osint, Zelensky). Weapons accounts conflict across outlets. | CLAIM ONLY |
| Repair date | No official timeline. Analysts say a year or more for the road span. | NOT ESTABLISHED |
| Crimea fuel | No fuel rationing or fuel-train report found. Rail, the fuel route, is running. | Absence, not a measured zero |

Sources: Kyiv Independent 11/16, 11/17 and 11/18 · AP via PBS 11/17 · Military.com 11/17 (Reuters, CNN, Vedomosti) · The Insider 11/17 · Moscow Times 11/17 a94281 · Militarnyi 11/17. Record: KB-OSPREY-290.

## 2. Trade-assessment read (for TERRY via you; I sent TERRY nothing directly)

- **The bridge supports no oil investment implication on its own.** The evidence implies little or no new loss of crude or products flows in the next weeks: the Kerch route was already shut to commercial shipping on the July report, and no oil volumes via Azov were found in any source read. The horizon is the 1-3 months the channel takes to clear. **Invalidation:** a Russian notice clearing the channel quickly, or evidence that oil cargoes were still moving through the strait under permits (Reuters reported grain permits from Temryuk and Kavkaz valid 10/26-11/15). **Unknown:** whether the July stop was still in force on 11/16, and the pre-closure oil volumes. **Grain is the larger exposure** (SovEcon: up to 25% of Russian grain exports used the route). That is outside my domain, so I name it to you for the owner.
- **The refinery campaign continues to tighten Russian products, not crude.** There are 12 refinery rows in November, and four of them fall on 11/15-11/18. Moscow Times reports Russia urging lower-grade gasoline; a Bloomberg title says diesel exports drop; a Quartz title says crude exports are the highest since July. The read is products pressure over the next 2-6 weeks. **Invalidation:** an energy or maritime moratorium at the 11/19 Shenzhen meeting, or monthly runs at 4.5 M bpd or more (OSP-10). **Unknown:** barrels lost. These are CAPACITY figures, not barrels, and no halt is reported at any of the four new sites. BRENT owns the prices and cracks.
